formula.title: Case Transformation & Tokenization Rules
formula.explanation: Input strings are tokenized into words using Unicode letter property escapes (\p{L}). Words are then restructured according to specific style rules: Chicago Manual of Style minor word rules for Title Case, or underscore/hyphen delimiters for programmatic identifiers.

commonMistakes.title: Capitalizing Minor Prepositions in Title Case
commonMistakes.description: In Chicago and AP style, minor prepositions, articles, and conjunctions under four letters (e.g., 'in', 'on', 'the', 'and', 'for') remain lowercase unless starting a sentence.

commonMistakes.title: Breaking Unicode & Accented Characters
commonMistakes.description: Naive case conversion using standard ASCII regex fails on accented letters like 'é' or non-Latin alphabets; Unicode property escapes (\p{L}) must be used.

commonMistakes.title: Losing Delimiters When Converting Code
commonMistakes.description: Converting camelCase or snake_case code into sentence case strips programming delimiters. Keep backups or use the Undo button.

commonMistakes.title: Title Case on All-Caps Input
commonMistakes.description: If all-caps text is fed into a title case engine without initial lower-casing, minor prepositions remain capitalized. Our algorithm normalizes tokens first.

faqs.q: How do you convert text case online?
faqs.a: Paste your text into the converter box and click any case transformation button such as UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case, or Sentence case. The text updates immediately in your browser.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Title Case and Capitalize Each Word?
faqs.a: Title Case capitalizes primary words but keeps minor grammatical articles and prepositions (such as 'in', 'the', 'of', 'and', 'for') in lowercase unless they appear as the first or last word. Capitalize Each Word unconditionally capitalizes the first letter of every single word.

faqs.q: What is the difference between camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, and kebab-case?
faqs.a: camelCase starts lowercase and capitalizes subsequent words with no spaces (e.g. 'myVariable'). PascalCase capitalizes all words including the first ('MyVariable'). snake_case separates words with underscores in lowercase ('my_variable'). kebab-case separates words with hyphens ('my-variable').

faqs.q: Can I undo a conversion if I don't like the result?
faqs.a: Yes. Click the Undo button to revert to your previous text state at any time.

faqs.q: Is my text data private when using the converter?
faqs.a: Yes. All text transformation logic executes strictly in local browser memory via client-side JavaScript. Your text is never stored in URLs, never saved to cookies, and never sent to remote servers.

faqs.q: Does the converter support foreign languages and accented characters?
faqs.a: Yes. The text engine uses Unicode property escapes (\p{L}) to handle accents, umlauts, and international alphabets like Spanish, French, and German seamlessly.
CONSTANT_CASE converts text to uppercase with underscores, the standard naming convention for global variables, immutable constants, and environment variables in programming.
